clean_source_blocks.text: The Flamingo Air plane had taken off from Lynden Pindling International Airport Nine passengers and a pilot have died in a small plane crash in the Bahamas, officials said. The light aircraft was making a short trip from Lynden Pindling International Airport, near capital Nassau, San Andros Airport when it "reportedly encountered difficulties" and crashed into bushes prior to landing, the country's Aircraft Accident Investigation Authority said in a statement. The fatal crash is occurred on the day of the Bahamas' 53rd independence anniversary. "Today is a day ​of celebration but it has become a ⁠day of mourning," Prime Minister Philip Davis told a media conference. He added: "Once again, a chapter in our nation's story has been marked by tragedy."
The country's prime minister called the crash, on the country's independence day, a tragedy.

A small plane crashed in the Bahamas on Friday, killing 10 people and prompting the government to temporarily ground Flamingo Air flights. The deadly incident happened in North Andros, located in waters just west of Nassau, the archipelago's capital. Bahamian Prime Minister Philip Brave Davis had initially said that one person survived, but he later confirmed in a press conference that the person died from their injuries. The victims have not been publicly identified. “We gather beneath a cloud of great sorrow,” he said, noting that people were celebrating the Bahamas' 53rd independence anniversary. “It has become a day of mourning. ... To every family that has received the devastating news, that someone they love will not be coming home, we offer our deepest condolences."

Bahamian Prime Minister Philip Brave Davis had initially said that one person survived, but he later confirmed in a news conference that the person died from their injuries. "We gather beneath a cloud of great sorrow," he said, noting that people were celebrating the Bahamas' 53rd independence anniversary. "It has become a day of mourning. ... To every family that has received the devastating news, that someone they love will not be coming home, we offer our deepest condolences." The Bahamian Aircraft Accident Investigation Authority said in a statement that the plane had departed Lynden Pindling International Airport in Nassau and was headed to San Andros when it crashed. It identified the plane as a Cessna 402 aircraft registered in the Bahamas.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
The Flamingo Air plane had taken off from Lynden Pindling International Airport

Nine passengers and a pilot have died in a small plane crash in the Bahamas, officials said.

The light aircraft was making a short trip from Lynden Pindling International Airport, near capital Nassau, San Andros Airport when it "reportedly encountered difficulties" and crashed into bushes prior to landing, the country's Aircraft Accident Investigation Authority said in a statement.

The fatal crash is occurred on the day of the Bahamas' 53rd independence anniversary.

"Today is a day ​of celebration but it has become a ⁠day of mourning," Prime Minister Philip Davis told a media conference.

He added: "Once again, a chapter in our nation's story has been marked by tragedy."

Davis initially said there was one survivor, although he confirmed hours later that the person had died from their injuries.

The details of the people on board, including their age and names, have not been released.

TheCessna 402 aircraft ​was operated by ​Flamingo Air, ⁠a Bahamas-based airline. The Ministry of Aviation said it was temporarily suspending ​the airline's air operator certificate "as a precautionary ​safety ⁠measure."

The grounding measure "should not be treated as an adverse compliance action against Flamingo Air," the ministry said.

It noted there had been "two safety incidents" that had occurred on Friday.

Aviation Minister JoBeth Coleby-Davis told reporters a plane had earlier routed back to Nassau when the pilot reported an issue. A fire broke out on board once the aircraft landed and passengers had disembarked, the BBC's US partner CBS News reported.

The BBC has contacted Flamingo Air for comment.

In remarks to local media, the airline said: "At this time, the details are being gathered, and we are committed to cooperating with the relevant authorities."

---

[Lähde: NBC New York]
A small plane crashed in the Bahamas on Friday, killing 10 people and prompting the government to temporarily ground Flamingo Air flights.

The deadly incident happened in North Andros, located in waters just west of Nassau, the archipelago's capital.

Bahamian Prime Minister Philip Brave Davis had initially said that one person survived, but he later confirmed in a press conference that the person died from their injuries. The victims have not been publicly identified.

“We gather beneath a cloud of great sorrow,” he said, noting that people were celebrating the Bahamas' 53rd independence anniversary. “It has become a day of mourning. ... To every family that has received the devastating news, that someone they love will not be coming home, we offer our deepest condolences."

The Bahamian Aircraft Accident Investigation Authority said in a statement that the plane had departed Lynden Pindling International Airport in Nassau and was headed to San Andros when it crashed. It identified the plane as a Cessna 402 aircraft registered in the Bahamas.

The Ministry of Energy, Utilities and Aviation said in a statement that the suspension of Flamingo Air’s air operator certificate is only a precautionary safety measure as officials investigate the cause of the crash. The ministry said the suspension is a result of two safety incidents that happened Friday.

During the press conference, Energy, Utilities and Aviation Minister JoBeth Coleby-Davis said the first incident occurred earlier Friday involving a Flamingo Air plane. She said it was en route to Mayaguana when the pilot reported a concern and turned back to Nassau. After the plane landed and the passengers deboarded, the plane caught fire, she said. That incident also is under investigation.

---

[Lähde: CBS News]
A small plane crashed in the Bahamas on Friday, killing several people and prompting the government to temporarily ground Flamingo Air flights.

The deadly incident happened in North Andros, located in waters just west of Nassau, the archipelago's capital.

Officials have not released details on those who were aboard or their conditions. Ten people were set to be on the flight, which departed from Nassau and crashed in Andros Island, according to a flight manifest obtained by CBS News.

While officials have not released a list of names, the manifest shows that members of the Da Pond Band — a musical group — were set to be on board, according to an aviation source.

Bahamian Prime Minister Philip Brave Davis had initially said that one person survived, but he later confirmed in a news conference that the person died from their injuries.

"We gather beneath a cloud of great sorrow," he said, noting that people were celebrating the Bahamas' 53rd independence anniversary. "It has become a day of mourning. ... To every family that has received the devastating news, that someone they love will not be coming home, we offer our deepest condolences."

The Bahamian Aircraft Accident Investigation Authority said in a statement that the plane had departed Lynden Pindling International Airport in Nassau and was headed to San Andros when it crashed. It identified the plane as a Cessna 402 aircraft registered in the Bahamas.

The Ministry of Energy, Utilities and Aviation said in a statement that the suspension of Flamingo Air's air operator certificate is only a precautionary safety measure as officials investigate the cause of the crash. The ministry said the suspension is a result of two safety incidents that happened Friday.

During the news conference, Energy, Utilities and Aviation Minister JoBeth Coleby-Davis said the first incident occurred earlier Friday involving a Flamingo Air plane. She said it was en route to Mayaguana when the pilot reported a concern and turned back to Nassau. After the plane landed and the passengers deboarded, the plane caught fire, she said. That incident is also under investigation.

        contributed to this report.

payload.title: Pienkone syöksyi maahan Bahamalla – kaikki kymmenen koneessa ollutta kuolivat
payload.summary: Flamingo Airin Cessna 402 putosi pensaikkoon ennen laskeutumista San Androsiin. Turmassa kuolivat koneen lentäjä ja yhdeksän matkustajaa.
payload.content:
Flamingo Airin pienkoneen maahansyöksy on surmannut Bahamalla kaikki kymmenen koneessa ollutta ihmistä. Viranomaisten mukaan perjantaina sattuneessa turmassa kuolivat lentäjä ja yhdeksän matkustajaa. Onnettomuus tapahtui Pohjois-Androsilla samana päivänä, jolloin saarivaltiossa vietettiin maan 53. itsenäisyyspäivää. Bahaman hallitus määräsi turman jälkeen lentoyhtiön lennot väliaikaisesti keskeytettäviksi.

## Kone putosi ennen laskeutumista

Bahamalle rekisteröity Cessna 402 oli lähtenyt Lynden Pindlingin kansainväliseltä lentoasemalta pääkaupunki Nassaun läheltä. Kone oli lyhyellä lennolla kohti San Androsin lentoasemaa. Bahaman lento-onnettomuuksia tutkivan viranomaisen mukaan kone joutui tiettävästi vaikeuksiin ja syöksyi pensaikkoon ennen kuin se ehti laskeutua määränpäähänsä.

Turma sattui Pohjois-Androsilla, joka sijaitsee saaristossa Nassaun länsipuolella. Viranomaiset eivät ole kertoneet tarkemmin, millaisia vaikeuksia kone kohtasi tai mikä johti maahansyöksyyn. Onnettomuustutkintaviranomaisen julkistamat tiedot vahvistavat koneen tyypin, lähtöpaikan, määränpään ja sen, että kone putosi juuri ennen suunniteltua laskeutumista. Turman tarkka syy ei käy ilmi julkaistuista tiedoista.

## Alustava tieto selviytyneestä muuttui

Pääministeri Philip Brave Davis kertoi aluksi, että yksi koneessa ollut ihminen olisi selvinnyt turmasta hengissä. Hän kuitenkin vahvisti myöhemmin tiedotustilaisuudessa, että kyseinen henkilö oli kuollut saamiinsa vammoihin. Lopulliseksi kuolonuhrien määräksi vahvistettiin siten kymmenen, eikä kukaan lennolla olleista selvinnyt onnettomuudesta. Uhrien henkilöllisyyksiä ei ole julkistettu.

Davisin mukaan Bahaman asukkaat olivat viettämässä maan 53. itsenäisyyspäivää, mutta juhlapäivä muuttui onnettomuuden vuoksi surupäiväksi. Hän kuvasi maata suuren surun varjostamaksi ja sanoi, että Bahaman kansalliseen tarinaan oli jälleen kirjoitettu tragedian leimaama luku.

## Hallitus keskeytti yhtiön lennot

Bahaman hallitus keskeytti Flamingo Airin lennot väliaikaisesti turman jälkeen. Lähdeaineistossa ei kerrota, kuinka kauan keskeytyksen on määrä jatkua tai mitä muita toimia lentoyhtiöön kohdistetaan. Pääministeri esitti osanottonsa perheille, jotka olivat saaneet tiedon siitä, ettei heidän läheisensä palaisi kotiin. Viranomaisten julkaisemien tietojen perusteella seuraavaksi on selvitettävä, mitä lennon loppuvaiheessa tapahtui ja mistä ennen laskeutumista ilmoitetut vaikeudet johtuivat.

Nassausta lähtenyt Cessna 402 putosi pensaikkoon ennen laskeutumista San Androsiin.
Bahaman hallitus keskeytti Flamingo Airin lennot väliaikaisesti onnettomuuden jälkeen.
